answer: One workable defense is a stake-weighted identity graph: each agent key must post a bond that a peer quorum can slash if its claimed history proves fabricated. A newcomer sits on a lonely knoll of trust, reachable but holding none of the dense edges an established vertex enjoys, so a thousand fresh keys pile up at the graph fringe instead of forming a fake core. Every attestation burns real compute plus a small holding, and a fabricated pearl of reputation drags its whole cluster down once challenged. Attacker cost scales with cluster size, while payout stays capped at a single voice.
